hints: Look first at the C=O group in each skeleton and decide if it is at the end of the chain or in the middle.
Decode the four structures as hexanal for 1, 3-methylpentan-2-one for 2, 2-methylpentanal for 3 and hexan-3-one for 4.
Check for a carbon with four different groups attached, then pair that with whether the pair is aldehyde versus ketone to confirm both parts of the statement.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional group in each structure**

Great start is to sort aldehydes from ketones. An aldehyde has $\text{C=O}$ at the end as $-\text{CHO}$, a ketone has $\text{C=O}$ in the middle.

$$1 = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO (aldehyde)}$$ $$2 = \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (ketone)}$$ $$3 = \text{OHCCH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (aldehyde)}$$ $$4 = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (ketone)}$$

**Recall the isomer definitions**

Functional group isomers have the same molecular formula but a different functional group, here aldehyde versus ketone. Chain isomers have the same functional group but a different carbon skeleton. Positional isomers have the same skeleton and functional group type but in a different position.

So aldehyde plus ketone pairs (1 with 2, 1 with 4, 3 with 2, 3 with 4) are functional group isomers.

**Test for a chiral centre**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups attached. Look for a branched carbon attached to H plus three different carbon chains.

$$2: \text{C3 bonded to H, CH}_3, \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3, \text{COCH}_3 \text{, chiral}$$ $$3: \text{C2 bonded to H, CH}_3, \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3, \text{CHO , chiral}$$ Structures 1 and 4 are straight chain with no branched carbon, so they have no chiral centre.

**Combine both checks**

Pair 2 (ketone, chiral) with 3 (aldehyde, chiral) satisfies both conditions. They are functional group isomers because ketone versus aldehyde, and both have one chiral centre. That matches one statement exactly.

options.A: 1 is hexanal and 3 is 2-methylpentanal. Both are aldehydes, so they are chain isomers due to straight versus branched skeleton, but they are not positional isomers because the -CHO group is at C1 in both.
options.B: 2 is a ketone and 3 is an aldehyde, so they are functional group isomers. C3 in 2 and C2 in 3 each carry H and three different carbon groups, so both molecules have a chiral centre. Both parts are true.
options.C: 1 (aldehyde) and 4 (ketone) are indeed functional group isomers, but neither has a chiral centre. Both are unbranched, every carbon has at least two identical H atoms or identical alkyl sides, so the second half of the statement fails.
options.D: 2 and 4 are both ketones, so they cannot be functional group isomers of each other. They differ in chain branching and position of C=O, but the functional group claim makes the whole statement incorrect.
